     Copper. Cu.

     A substance little known as a remedy before Hahnemann, although used by Mediæval physicians, after its introduction by Hohenheim (called Paracelsus) in the sixteenth century, and later (1845) in an empiric way by the Rademacherian School, in which it ranked as a polychrest.

     A comprehensive monograph, including the provings and observations of Hahnemann and his provers, Bœnninghausen, Stapf, Rückert, etc., with results of poisoning and curative symptoms, was published by C. Hering. In it the effects of the metal and the acetate are conjoined, on account of their similarity, but separated here, for the sake of individuality. See Cuprum aceticum.
